findings.where: Footer links: Privacy, Terms and Report content (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: All three links reload this same How we rank page (parts.txt p6, p7, p9). They look like working legal and reporting routes, but a visitor who clicks Privacy, Terms or Report content never reaches a privacy notice, terms or a way to report anything.
findings.who_objects: Both readers of this page will object. A backpacker or hostel owner checking whether the site is trustworthy finds the legal pages are fake. A hostel owner who wants to report a review has no route. On a page whose whole job is trust, links that go nowhere undo the claim.

findings.where: Nav bar: Destinations link (desktop inline; phone Menu panel)
findings.fault: Destinations links to #destinations on this page (parts.txt p3), but this page has no destinations section. The click goes nowhere, and the visitor's only route onward from this page is dead.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has read the method and now wants to look at hostels clicks Destinations and stays where they are. They are left on a page that ends on a competitor paragraph with no way forward.

findings.where: 'Hostelworld, for comparison' section, the last section on the page
findings.fault: The page ends on a paragraph that names Hostelworld and describes how its scores can mislead. The brief says the demand-side claim names no competitor and that Manta does not compete on review policing. Hostelworld is also a party whose consent Manta is still waiting on (#78). The section turns a method page into a dig at a competitor. The cited source is plain text, not a link a reader could check.
findings.who_objects: The founder will object: the positioning bars naming competitors, and the page risks the pending Hostelworld application. A backpacker who uses Hostelworld daily may read it as sniping rather than transparency.

findings.where: Intro lede ('This page states it in full') against the Ranking method's shrinkage paragraph
findings.fault: The lede promises the method 'in full'. The pull toward the area average is then described only in vague words: 'partway', 'a handful', 'a few dozen', 'its area'. The page gives no weights, no threshold and no worked example. The decay rule gets exact percentages; the shrinkage rule, which matters more for small hostels, gets none.
findings.who_objects: A sceptical hostel owner, or a backpacker comparing a 4-review hostel with a 200-review one, cannot check how far a score was pulled. The 'in full' claim reads as overstated, which is the opposite of what a trust page needs.

findings.where: Intro summary list item 1 and the first sentence of Ranking method
findings.fault: The strongest trust claim, 'No hostel can pay for a higher position', is set as a plain list item. It has the same weight as 'Recent stays count more than old ones' and is then repeated word for word as the first sentence of the next section. The loud claim is never made loud, and it is said twice instead of once with weight.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker skimming on a phone should take away 'rank can't be bought' in five seconds. As set, it sits flat among the method details and nothing on the page marks it as the point.

findings.where: Intro block: the lede, the smaller 'Scores weight toward recent stays…' paragraph, then the numbered list
findings.fault: There are three summary layers in a row. The smaller paragraph says the same as list items 2 and 3. The list is numbered (1, 2, 3) although the points are not steps or a ranking, so the numbers suggest an order that does not exist.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader mid-transit reads the same idea twice before reaching the method. The numbering implies priority or sequence where there is none.

findings.where: Ranking method section against Scoring method section
findings.fault: The headings do not group the content. Most of 'Ranking method' is about scoring: the pull toward the area average, which reviews count, and showing 'No reviews yet' at zero. 'Scoring method' then holds only the time decay.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who jumps to 'Scoring method' to learn how a score is made finds only the decay rule and misses the area-average pull, which sits under the ranking heading.

findings.where: Ranking method's four paragraphs (phone-01 most of all) and the Hostelworld paragraph
findings.fault: The text runs as long, unbroken paragraphs with no subheads, key terms or examples to scan by. On the phone, Ranking method is about two screens of solid text. Several sentences run well past 25 words; the Hostelworld paragraph's first sentence is about 75 words.
findings.who_objects: The primary reader is a backpacker on a phone, often mid-transit. They will not work through a two-screen wall to find out how reviews count, so the trust the page publishes goes unread.

findings.where: Whole page, desktop at 1440 px (desktop-01, desktop-02)
findings.fault: The single text column, about 520 px wide, sits hard left inside a 1050 px container. The right 60% of every screen is empty sand. The page looks lopsided and unfinished, not deliberately set as a reading column.
findings.who_objects: A hostel owner reading on a laptop after cold outreach sees a page that looks half-built, which works against the professional, trustworthy impression the page exists to give.

findings.fault: Apart from the nav and footer, the page is ink text on sand with nothing else: no illustration, no worked example, no visual for the decay or the pull toward the average. The brief names sterile and corporate as the enemy, and wants the loud claim backed by plain mechanics. Here there is no loud claim, only mechanics.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose north star is 'loud moments, calm machine' and whose first feeling is 'effortless'. A backpacker gets a legal-notice look on the one page meant to win their trust.

findings.where: Page as a whole: no date on the method
findings.fault: The page gives the date it read Hostelworld's help centre, but no date or version for Manta's own method. A visitor cannot tell whether the rules shown are the ones in force now.
findings.who_objects: A hostel owner whose rank changes, or a backpacker sceptical of a pre-launch site, wants to know the method is current. A published method with no date reads as undated boilerplate.

findings.fault: The '·' separator after 'How we rank' is left dangling at the end of the first line, and the row wraps with no separator at the start of the second.
findings.who_objects: Few would notice. A careful reader sees it as a stray mark, a small craft lapse in the brand's own chrome.
